Hi

About a year ago I posted a few questions relating to photopolymers. I was particularly interested in the 532nm sensitive polymer. One of the problems at that time was narrowband replay and therefore its use in display holography. It was also quite expensive to get from Sergio in Brazil.

I believe Sergio said that he was working on a polymer that would have much wider bandwidth. I just wondered if anyone (Sergio?) knew any more of this or if there had been any substantial developments in the last twelve months. I was also led to understand that there would be a European distributor, has anything happened with this?

I now have a 200mW 532nm SLM laser (C532-200) which I suspect would be ideal for use with photopolymer and I would like to give it a try if the costs are reasonable.

Sergio, if you read this can you let me know what film and liquid photopolymers are available in 532nm sensitive. If you have any links to datasheets that would be good.

Thanks

Jem

Hello Jem, thank you for your interest, I'm still working with this with Martin Mueller, first results were used for thin transmission gratings at sensitivity around 3mJ/cm² (532nm) with liquid photopolymers that indeed were even used without spaces, giving decent efficiency and even reflection grating capable. I have a report that could send you and a complete article is available below.

I also have experimental films based on modified polyurethane emulsion that I could arrange for you, with the aim of same sensitivity, please PM for me and I will verify what samples/format I could arrange for you maybe paying only the shipping package.

The solid film may be also available for glass "sandwich" forming after cure a transparent solid-gel film stable for reflection exposure for relatively thick films compared to thin liquid ones necessary for stability.

Actual commerce is made with interested partners for production HOE elements but other holographic midia producers are welcome.

*Proceedings Vol. 7138Photonics, Devices, and Systems IV, Pavel Tománek; Dagmar Senderáková; Miroslav Hrabovský, Editors, 71381EDate: 18 November 2008Paper AbstractHolography, holographic interferometry, or holographic optical elements manufacturing are compromised by the shortcomings of used holographic recording materials. Classical materials such as silver-halide emulsions, their excellent sensitivity, resolution, spectral range are eclipsed by the necessity of wet chemical processing and by inherent noise. Other commonly used holographic materials are not much better, some of their parameters are good however compromised with other weak parameters. Recently, it has seemed that new properly designed and manufactured photopolymer recording materials can overcome most of these problems. The sandwich structure (glass-polymer-glass) of the recording media can be easily prepared from commercial available liquid photopolymers (Polygrama) and well balanced holographic recording media are obtained by this approach. This paper presents testing results and preliminary conclusions of sandwich photopolymer structures employed as a holographic recording media. Characterization of recording structures as well as real life holographic usage examples are done. Influence of development and hardening of photopolymer are shown. Innovative formula of used photopolymer enables easily to reach diffraction efficiency of structures close to 100 % with low dose of exposition energy.DOI: 10.1117/12.818035Current SPIE Digital Library subscribers click here to download this paper.© SPIE - Downloading of the abstract is permitted for personal use only.See Terms of Use*
